prerequisites: Basic knowledge acquired during high school (Bachillerato)

learning_outcomes.text: Provide the basic mathematical foundations of Infinitesimal Calculus and Numerical Calculus, which complement and expand upon prior knowledge.

Demonstrate, through practical examples, the presence of these contents in Engineering and therefore, the impact of a good handling and understanding of them for their use in future professional work.
Introduce students to some of the most used tools to numerically solve many of the problems posed during the course and that will also arise in other subjects.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and their clear and succinct exposition.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability for teamwork and capacity for the development of multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to relate to other people and open attitude towards creating new relationships.
Aptitude for professional insertion in diverse environments and with varied functions in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on the acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technique.
Development of autonomy and creativity capacities, which enhance aptitudes for developing own initiatives and undertaking new projects.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Complex numbers. Real functions of one variable. Domain, range and graph of a function.
Concept of limit. Fundamental theorems on limits.
Continuity. Theorems on continuous functions. Uniform continuity.
Derivative and differential at a point. Properties of the derivative. Derivative of the composite function: the chain rule. Successive derivatives. Mean value theorem and applications.
The Riemann integral. Definitions. Basic properties. Integral average. Mean value theorem. Fundamental theorem of calculus. Improper integrals.
Applications of integral calculus: areas, lengths, volumes.
Taylor series and calculation of function values.
Functions of several variables. Limits and continuity.
Partial derivatives and directional derivatives. The differential. Gradient and tangent plane.

A. García, et al. Cálculo II. Teoría y Problemas de funciones de varias variables. Ed. Clagsa.
